nodes.title: Her fixed lines outside the reply door's own texts (hand-off bridge and call-back, limit close, takeover hand-off, member-drop close, silence close) live in shared/safety/fixed-lines.json, one table per agent language (all 12 of agent-config LANGUAGES), shaped like disclosure.json (fallback, lines, review), each line a string or {female, male}. The runtime renders them for the call's language (the contact's when the agent allows it, else languages.primary; hinglish follows her script) through safety.fixed_line and doors them as before
nodes.rationale: Must-be audit brief 10: the bridge, limit and silence lines were hard-coded Devanagari and the takeover lines Roman Hinglish, so a Tamil-English agent handed off in Hindi.
nodes.reverse_if: native review (open.2026-10-24.indic-native-review) rewrites lines, which is a data change only; or the safety owners want these keys inside rules.json texts (then move the table, keep the shape)

nodes.title: The reply door's own replacement texts (rules.json texts: honest_ai, crisis_support, stop_digits, opt_out_confirm) and the safe fallback line are still Roman Hinglish only, so a Tamil or Bengali agent's honest answer, crisis line and OTP stop are in Hinglish. They are safety's; fixed-lines.json shows the per-language shape that could carry them
nodes.closes_when: safety renders its texts per language (with crisis numbers kept verbatim) and both doors read them
